metrics.name: Realized hours per phone per working day
metrics.def: Accepted hours, the ones we are paid for, that one deployed phone produced on a day its site ran a shift.
metrics.how: Accepted hours for the day divided by phones deployed at sites that ran a shift that day. Recorded hours do not count until review keeps them.
metrics.owner: Mano, in the evening number. Hours from the wrap reports, verdicts from Youssef Medhat.
metrics.read: The shift is the ceiling. The month's target divided by deployed phones and working days is the floor. Under the floor, check active versus deployed first, then flags: one says phones sat, the other says footage was thrown away.

metrics.name: Backlog in device-days
metrics.def: Footage recorded but not yet uploaded, counted in phones holding a full day of it.
metrics.how: For each phone at the site, the footage it still holds as a share of a day's shift. Add them up. Two phones each holding half a day is one device-day.
metrics.owner: The Portfolio Manager, per site, in the wrap report. Hub attendants log devices held each night.
metrics.read: Zero after the flush is good. Over one at any site is an incident: Moharam hears the same night, and no device sleeps holding more than a day.

metrics.name: Flags per 1,000 hours
metrics.def: Review notes per thousand hours uploaded. A flag is one note on one video, feedback or fraud.
metrics.how: Flags in the week divided by hours uploaded in the week, times 1,000. Feedback and fraud on separate lines, then together.
metrics.owner: Youssef Medhat, weekly, by site and by worker.
metrics.read: Falling week over week is good. Rising at one site is a site problem. Rising everywhere is a briefing problem. A worker's own count matters more than any rate: a second strike pauses the device, three flags pulls the worker, and a fraud flag is footage nobody is paid for.

metrics.name: Catch-before-client rate
metrics.def: Of every video that ends up flagged, the share our own review caught before the client saw it.
metrics.how: Videos we flagged or deleted, divided by those plus the videos the client flagged after we passed them.
metrics.owner: Youssef Medhat, monthly, before the invoice. The client's flags come through Adham; nobody else talks to the client.
metrics.read: Good is all of them: the client finds nothing we missed. Every client flag is a miss. A catch costs the video. A miss costs the video and puts the account at risk.

metrics.name: Active phones versus deployed
metrics.def: Deployed phones are on the registry at a site. Active phones uploaded today. The gap is phones that sat.
metrics.how: Phones with an upload today divided by phones on the registry at that site today. Spares in the pool are not deployed. Partner phones count the same way.
metrics.owner: The Portfolio Manager, per site, in the wrap report. The quartermaster keeps the deployed count true.
metrics.read: Good is every deployed phone active. A phone dark by noon gets a visit from its anchor, and the Portfolio Manager hears the same hour. The fleet short at 6 PM is a same-night call, not a next-morning conversation.

metrics.name: Hours by environment category
metrics.def: Accepted hours split by the kind of place they were filmed in: factory, hotel, warehouse, construction site, farm.
metrics.how: Every site carries one environment tag from sourcing. Add its accepted hours to that line.
metrics.owner: Mano, weekly, in the numbers behind the client update and the sourcing target list.
metrics.read: There is no good total, only a good mix. Sites are chosen for the categories they add, not just the hours. A line that stops growing is where the next site goes.
